title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. 2.1
Traditional Imputation Methods
Missing data imputation has been extensively studied across vari-
ous domains. The simplest approach is mean imputation, which re-
places missing values with the feature mean for numerical variables
or mode for categorical variables [7, 14]. While computationally
efficient, this method fails to preserve the natural variability of data
and can lead to biased estimates when missing data is not random.
K-nearest neighbors (KNN) [3] imputation estimates missing

The Expectation-Maximization (EM) [8] algorithm provides a
principled statistical approach to impute missing values based on
maximum likelihood density estimation. However, EM requires
strong distributional assumptions that may not hold in practice and
can converge to local optima.
Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) [19] ex-
tends single imputation by creating multiple imputed datasets and
combining results to account for imputation uncertainty. MICE can
handle mixed-type data and complex missing patterns but requires
careful specification of imputation models for each variable and
can be computationally expensive.
Tree-based methods like MissForest [17] employ random forests

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (re-implementation from the paper).

Reference: "Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data"
(Sections 4.1-4.3).  All steps follow the equations in the paper:

* Eq. (4)  equal-frequency bin centers = evenly spaced percentiles of the
           *observed* values of each feature, with the first/last center at the
           min / max (percentiles 0 and 100).
* Eq. (5)  proximity assignment: each observed value goes to the nearest center.
* Eq. (6)-(7) one-hot encoding of every observed feature, concatenated over
           features to build z_i.
* Eq. (8)-(14) three-level cascading fallback for the encodings of missing
           features: intersection matching -> union matching -> global prior.
* Eq. (15)-(16) proximity kernel K = (1/d) Z Z^T.

The mask computations use Python big integers as bitsets so that the exact
set operations of Eqs. (8)-(12) stay cheap even for ~50k samples.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def _percentile_centers(obs: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Evenly spaced percentiles of the observed values (Eq. 4).

    Positions are (k-1)*100/(nbins-1) for k=1..nbins, so that the extreme
    centers are the min and the max of the feature (as stated after Eq. 4).
    """
    if nbins == 1:
        return np.array([float(np.mean(obs))])
    qs = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins)
    return np.percentile(obs, qs)


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int, center_rule: str = "paper_eq4") -> list:
    """Return a list of per-feature bin-center arrays (None if fully missing)."""
    d = X.shape[1]
    centers = []
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            continue
        if center_rule == "paper_eq4":
            c = _percentile_centers(obs, nbins)
        elif center_rule == "inner_percentiles":
            # alternative rule recorded in the plan (percentiles k/(nbins+1))
            c = np.percentile(obs, 100.0 * np.arange(1, nbins + 1) / (nbins + 1))
        elif center_rule == "left_edges":
            c = np.percentile(obs, 100.0 * np.arange(0, nbins) / nbins)
        else:
            raise ValueError(center_rule)
        centers.append(np.asarray(c, dtype=float))
    return centers


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers: list, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Proximity assignment (Eq. 5).  Missing entries get -1.

    Ties are broken towards the lowest bin index by ``argmin``.
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=np.int64)
    for j in range(d):
        obs_mask = ~np.isnan(X[:, j])
        c = centers[j]
        if c is None:
            continue
        xv = X[obs_mask, j][:, None]
        B[obs_mask, j] = np.argmin(np.abs(xv - c[None, :]), axis=1)
    return B


class ProximityKernel:
    """Build the sparse/fractional representation Z of the proximity kernel."""

    def __init__(self, nbins: int, center_rule: str = "paper_eq4",
                 fallback_norm: str = "observed"):
        self.nbins = int(nbins)
        self.center_rule = center_rule
        self.fallback_norm = fallback_norm  # "observed" | "S_size"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ fit
    def fit_transform(self, X: np.ndarray):
        """Return Z (n, d*nbins) and a diagnostics dictionary."""
        X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
        n, d = X.shape
        nb = self.nbins

"""Ensure the UCI raw files used by the reproduction exist in the shared cache.

Only the files that are actually needed by ``reproduce.py`` are required; every
other download is best-effort (a 404 just prints a warning).  The primary target

import os
import sys
import urllib.request

CACHE = os.environ.get(
    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE",
    os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".cache", "datasets", "files"),
)
DEST = os.path.join(CACHE, "uci")
UCI = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/"

FILES = {
    "hepatitis.data": UCI + "hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
    "mammographic_masses.data": UCI + "mammographic-masses/mammographic_masses.data",
    "breast-cancer-wisconsin.data": UCI + "breast-cancer-wisconsin/breast-cancer-wisconsin.data",
    "agaricus-lepiota.data": UCI + "mushroom/agaricus-lepiota.data",
    "house-votes-84.data": UCI + "voting-records/house-votes-84.data",
    "crx.data": UCI + "credit-screening/crx.data",
    "adult.data": UCI + "adult/adult.data",
    "soybean-large.data": UCI + "soybean/soybean-large.data",
    "primary-tumor.data": UCI + "primary-tumor/primary-tumor.data",
    "heart.dat": UCI + "statlog/heart/heart.dat",
    "chronic_kidney_disease.arff": UCI + "chronic_kidney_disease/chronic_kidney_disease.arff",
}
REQUIRED = ["hepatitis.data"]


def present(name: str) -> bool:
    p = os.path.join(DEST, name)
    return os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p) > 0


def fetch(name: str) -> bool:
    os.makedirs(DEST, exist_ok=True)
    if present(name):
        return True
    url = FILES[name]
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
            blob = r.read()
        with open(os.path.join(DEST, name), "wb") as f:
            f.write(blob)
        print(f"[download] {name} <- {url} ({len(blob)} bytes)")
        return True
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - downloads are best effort
        print(f"[download] WARNING could not fetch {name} from {url}: {exc}")
        return False


def ensure(names):
    return {n: fetch(n) for n in names}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    wanted = sys.argv[1:] or list(FILES)
    ok = ensure(wanted)
    if any(not ok[n] for n in REQUIRED if n in wanted):
        raise SystemExit("a required data file is missing from the cache")

"""K-means clustering + NMI evaluation and the nbins search (paper Sec. 5.1)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

from .proximity_kernel import ProximityKernel

NBINS_GRID = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]           # paper Sec. 5.1 hyperparameter search
SEEDS = list(range(10))                # "each experiment conducted 10 times"


def evaluate_seeds(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=SEEDS, n_init=10):
    """K-means with the ground-truth number of clusters; NMI per seed."""
    nmis = []
    for seed in seeds:
        km = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init,
                    random_state=seed)
        labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
        nmis.append(float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)))
    nmis = np.asarray(nmis)
    return {"mean": float(nmis.mean()), "std": float(nmis.std(ddof=0)),
            "per_seed": [float(v) for v in nmis]}


def run_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, nbins, seeds=SEEDS, center_rule="paper_eq4",
              fallback_norm="observed", n_init=10):
    pk = ProximityKernel(nbins=nbins, center_rule=center_rule,
                         fallback_norm=fallback_norm)
    Z, diag = pk.fit_transform(X)
    res = evaluate_seeds(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds=seeds, n_init=n_init)
    res.update({"nbins": int(nbins), "Z_shape": [int(s) for s in Z.shape],
                "diagnostics": diag})
    return res, pk


def search_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, grid=NBINS_GRID, seeds=SEEDS,
                 center_rule="paper_eq4", fallback_norm="observed", n_init=10):
    """Search nbins; the reported value is the best mean NMI over the grid."""
    per_nbins = []
    for nb in grid:
        res, _ = run_nbins(X, y, n_clusters, nb, seeds=seeds,
                           center_rule=center_rule, fallback_norm=fallback_norm,
                           n_init=n_init)
        per_nbins.append(res)
        print(f"  nbins={nb}: mean NMI {res['mean']:.4f} +- {res['std']:.4f}")
    means = [r["mean"] for r in per_nbins]
    best = int(np.argmax(means))
    return {"best_nbins": per_nbins[best]["nbins"], "best_mean": per_nbins[best]["mean"],
            "best_std": per_nbins[best]["std"],
            "best_per_seed": per_nbins[best]["per_seed"],
            "selected_by": "max mean NMI over 10 seeds (assumption A9)",
            "per_nbins": per_nbins}

    ],
}
for key, urls in cands.items():
    for url in urls:
        name = url.split("/")[-1]
        out = os.path.join(DEST, name)
        if os.path.exists(out) and os.path.getsize(out) > 0:
            print("cached", name, os.path.getsize(out))
            continue
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
                blob = r.read()
            if name.endswith(".zip"):
                with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(blob)) as z:
                    print(key, "zip members:", z.namelist())
                    z.extractall(os.path.join(DEST, key))
            else:
                with open(out, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(blob)
                print("ok", name, len(blob))
        except Exception as exc:
            print("FAIL", url, exc)

audit_summary: The clean re-run recomputes Hepatitis NMI = 0.228909 from raw UCI data, essentially identical to the paper's 0.2289 (absolute deviation 9.1e-6), well inside the 0.02 tolerance. The implementation follows the proposed proximity kernel: per-feature observed-value percentile centers, nearest-center assignment, one-hot concatenation, three-level fallback using kernel mean embedding/prior, and K=ZZ^T/d followed by ground-truth-K K-means with 10 seeds and NMI. The only material fidelity caveats are the disclosed A8/A14 restriction of the kernel-mean-embedding sums to matching samples that observe the missing feature, and the use of an extreme-inclusive percentile rule (A13) chosen from the paper's post-Eq.(4) text. The reported 0.2289 is selected as the best mean over the paper's nbins grid (nbins=2), which is disclosed and consistent with the paper's 'search' wording. requirement_check.evidence: src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins loops over each feature and computes centers from X[~np.isnan(...), j], so only observed values are used.
_percentile_centers uses np.linspace(0,100,nbins) and np.percentile, giving evenly spaced percentiles from min to max; this follows the paper sentence after Eq. (4) and assumption A13.
assign_bins uses np.argmin(abs(x - centers)), giving nearest-center Voronoi assignment; ties resolve to lowest index as documented (A3).
Observed entries are placed in H[i,j,bin]=1 and Z is H.reshape(n, d*nbins), producing the concatenated one-hot representation of Eqs. (6)-(7).
The missing-entry loop computes S1, then S2, then falls back to self.prior[j]; diagnostics report level1/level2/level3 counts.

Level 1 uses cand = S1(i) intersected with samples observing feature j and averages their one-hot bins (A8/A14). This is a defensible fix for undefined h_{m,j}, but it means level 1 can be skipped even when raw S1(i) is nonempty if no S1 member observes j.

Level 2 uses S2(i) intersected with samples observing feature j. The union fallback exists, but the trigger is 'no level-1 candidate observing j' rather than literally S1(i) empty, again following A8/A14.
When neither local set yields an observed-j candidate, H[i,j] is set to self.prior[j], the observed-bin frequency prior (uniform if the feature is fully missing), matching Eq. (14).
kernel() returns (Z @ Z.T)/d, i.e. the normalized inner product of Eq. (15).
src/cluster.py runs sklearn KMeans with n_clusters set to len(np.unique(y)) and scores labels with normalized_mutual_info_score.
SEEDS = list(range(10)); evaluate_seeds averages NMI over all 10 seeds and metrics.json stores per-seed values.
NBINS_GRID = [2,3,4,6,8] is searched for Hepatitis, and metrics.json records every grid entry.

The implementation uses per-sample Python big-integer bitsets for S1/S2 operations; no scaling benchmark is provided, so the paper's O(nd + d n log n) claim is not independently demonstrated for large n.
For fully observed rows every feature contributes exactly one 1 in H; Z has exactly d ones out of d*nbins entries, as checked by the encoding-sum assertions.
